content:
STAGE: read evidence bundle and scope-check all four proposals.
GOAL: confirm every proposal is in scope (behaviour+hyperbolic+coupling+testable+spec) and find evidence that discriminates them.
READ: frozen bundles for CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN (9637a2495b60c669), CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ (634a0d7731a5d022), CURVCHART-RESGUARD (dfec9cb5b35ea444), CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL (6476469bc16f6590); shared E1-E13.
OBSERVED: all four name a train-only transition signal, an explicit Poincare/Lorentz operation and the switchable both-on/off pathway, so none is out of scope. Discriminating evidence: (a) E6/E7 show residual/geometry-only variants already measured - tangent_successor_residual recall@10 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, all at/below frozen baseline 0.055537, with NLL profiles 4.00/3.17/1.67/0.29 - a direct prior for CURVEBEND's residual-direction bend. (b) E6 shows the level-1 collapse variant l1_br recall 0.04671 (T4 NLL 9.03, gold prefix alive depth1 1.000) versus l1_br_euclid 0.06207 and l1_only 0.06233 with gold alive depth2 0.829, i.e. spreading level 1 recovers ~0.015 recall. (c) E8 capacity ceiling K=256 0.0822 vs K=16 0.3106 shows resolution/partition granularity is the live lever. (d) E11 same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 leaves headroom for behaviour-aware prefixes.
REASONING: E6/E7 rule CURVEBEND down (its exact residual-bend family was already run and flat). The collapse-repair evidence favours mechanisms that structurally force/keep code usage wide: EQUIMARGIN's hard uniform marginals and CAP's frozen Euclidean capacity both do this. RESGUARD's 0.5-2x guard band is an explicitly admitted near-no-op risk with non-derived constants.
OPEN: need final ordering between EQUIMARGIN and CAP, and place RESGUARD vs CURVEBEND.

STAGE: compare resolution-safety, constant derivation, cost and expected effect; fix ordering.
READ: proposal specifications + E6/E7/E8/E11 + round-1 failure numbers cited in each motivation (2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, recall 0.041888 vs frozen 0.055537, support 247/7414/20223).
OBSERVED: EQUIMARGIN leaves the code table byte-identical, derives kappa_0 = 1/s_l^2 from measured residual RMS, adds an automatic alpha-halving safeguard triggered by measured U_l<0.9K_l, needs 8 documented null shuffles, costs +3-6% step time and one fixed-shape collective. CAP freezes column marginals to Euclidean counts (safer distribution than uniform but preserves any baseline imbalance) at 1.0-1.8x RQ step cost; its support-preservation claim is inexact because an argmax of a soft Sinkhorn plan does not reproduce the column marginals exactly. RESGUARD is cheap and codebook-preserving but clips each score to [0.5,2]x neutral, a hardcoded band, and its own hypothesis concedes <0.5% assignment change would make it a no-op. CURVEBEND only bends residual direction and is the family E6 already measured at 0.05500.
REASONING: EQUIMARGIN best matches the measured lever (spreading the collapsed level 1 raised beam recall to 0.06207 in E6) and is the most fully specified/cost-feasible; CAP is second because its capacity-freeze targets the same resolution goal but is more likely a pure reordering/no-op and costs more; RESGUARD third (bounded perturbation, non-derived band, admitted no-op risk); CURVEBEND last (directly contradicted by E6/E7 residual-geometry results).
OPEN: none. Ranking EQUIMARGIN=1, CAP=2, RESGUARD=3, CURVEBEND=4.

FINAL ANSWER (complete, ranking of all four proposals best-first):
RANK: CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN-RQ | position=1 | reason=E6/E7 show the collapsed level-1 variant l1_br at recall 0.04671 (T4 NLL 9.03) versus l1_br_euclid 0.06207 with gold alive depth2 0.829, and this is the only proposal whose hard uniform Sinkhorn marginals force U_l>=0.9K_l by construction, with derived kappa_0=1/s_l^2, an automatic measured-usage safeguard, code table left byte-identical, and only +3-6% step cost.
RANK: CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN | position=2 | reason=It targets the same resolution failure (round-1 2/13/56 SIDs, collision 0.998, 0.041888 vs 0.055537) by freezing column marginals to Euclidean counts and moving curvature onto per-pair c_ik=c_l*exp(-a_ik), consistent with E11's 0.0907 vs 0.067 prefix headroom, but its own risk says assignment change may be <1% and its exact support-preservation claim fails because argmax of a soft plan need not reproduce column marginals.
RANK: CURVCHART-RESGUARD | position=3 | reason=It is grounded in the same round-1 radius collapse and E8's K=256 0.0822 capacity ceiling, but it clips every chart score to a hardcoded [0.5,2]x neutral band and its own hypothesis concedes that <0.5% assignment change makes it a no-op, so it is the weakest live perturbation of the codebook-preserving proposals.
RANK: CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL | position=4 | reason=Its residual-direction bend is the mechanism family already measured in E6/E7: tangent_successor_residual recall@10 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500 and successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463 all sit at or below the frozen 0.055537 baseline, so the evidence directly contradicts the expected recall gain.

GOAL: read the four frozen evidence bundles and the shared probes before ranking. READ: all four bundles (9637a2495b60c669, 634a0d7731a5d022, dfec9cb5b35ea444, 6476469bc16f6590). OBSERVED: all four are IN SCOPE (behaviour signal + explicit curved op + one coupled pathway + three switches + cost). Frozen baseline Stage3 recall@10 0.055537, support 247/7414/20223; prior radius-spending round collapsed to 2/13/56, collision 0.998, L1 hit 0.982/0.980, recall 0.041888. Key probes: E8 K=16/32/64/256 pair-sharing 0.3106/0.2164/0.1547/0.0822; E6 best width-20 recall 0.06363 (resample), 0.06233 (l1_only), 0.06207 (l1_br_euclid), while successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500; E7 good-config NLL 0/3.22/4.36/1.23 (T3 hardest); E11 same-first-prefix 0.0907 vs null 0.067. STILL OPEN: final ordering.

GOAL: place the four proposals against the probes. REASONING: (a) CURVEBEND-NORM-RESIDUAL acts only on levels 2-3 where E7 shows the NLL bottleneck (T3=4.36, T4=1.23), keeps level 1 Euclidean so it cannot worsen E8's K=256 first-level capacity ceiling, preserves residual norm and the whole codebook so the 247/7414/20223 export is safe, and is the cheapest (0.2-0.5% step). Caution: E6 tangent_successor_residual already scored 0.05500. (b) CURVCHART-RESGUARD puts a statistically stable per-code curvature on the 24556-node item graph (more data per code than sparse prefix quotients), keeps the codebook byte-identical, and the [0.5,2] guard band bounds regression; but bounded perturbations are the family that E6 successor_geodesic_coarse/v2 already sat at ~0.055. (c) CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN forces 256-way uniform usage: it misreads the inherited baseline as collapsed (247/256 already alive, the 2/256 was the failed prior arm), so it has no resolution headroom, and forcing uniform 256 directly contradicts E8 (K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822) which is what width-20 prefix survival needs; also heaviest machinery with 20-epoch lag. (d) CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN freezes column marginals to the Euclidean counts, so it only permutes items within the same K=256 capacity ceiling and cannot coarsen; the argmax of a coupling does not actually preserve those marginals; it is the most expensive (up to 1.8x step) and its family is the one E6 shows at baseline. STILL OPEN: whether CURVCAP or EQUIMARGIN is last.

GOAL: finalise order. DECISION: CURVCAP last because it combines no granularity change (E8 ceiling untouched), a broken capacity-guarantee (argmax of a Sinkhorn coupling need not reproduce the column counts), and the highest cost; EQUIMARGIN third because although hard uniform marginals could echo the best probe (resample 0.06363) it is built on a misdiagnosis (baseline is not collapsed) and its uniformisation runs against E8. Final order: 1 CURVEBEND, 2 CURVCHART-RESGUARD, 3 CURVCHART-EQUIMARGIN, 4 CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN. This is the complete answer; no ablation/model run is needed for the review.
